world.hero.eyebrow: WORLD ATLAS · ONE CITY, REMEMBERED TWICE
world.hero.title2: They learned another way to live.
world.hero.body: Every match contains the same 12 memories, but never the same route map. After the Explosion Reset, Darkforest reinterprets Mega City's functions, dangers, and power structures.
world.topology.title: Remember places, not routes.
world.topology.note: This illustrates the generation rules, not the current match map. All 12 sites appear, but their positions, connections, and blockade order are rebuilt each match.
world.phases.title: The explosion does not replace the map. It changes what the same wound means.
world.phases.before.title: Civilization is still pretending to function
world.phases.before.body: Power, logistics, broadcasting, and class assign every space a purpose. Danger usually hides beneath clean surfaces and orderly systems.
world.phases.reset.title: Keep your choices. Rewrite their value.
world.phases.reset.body: Legacy and event traces remain. Two old routes collapse, two root paths open, and Echoes return carrying intelligence.
world.phases.after.title: Nature takes over the city's skeleton
world.phases.after.body: Pipes become rootways; platforms become tree bridges. Familiar Landmarks remain, but the advantages you knew can no longer be trusted.
world.atlas.eyebrow: 12 MEMORY PAIRS · ALL APPEAR EVERY MATCH
world.atlas.title: One landmark. Two ways to read survival.
world.atlas.body: Names and environmental character stay fixed; positions and connections do not. These are world records, not a route guide for your current match.
world.place.rootheart.story: The city once treated the crimson root as a mechanical organ for moving energy. After the blast, real roots followed the old pipes and began preserving every memory left unfinished.
world.place.rootheart.tactic: Both eras are cramped: tools and cleavers have room to work, while rifles struggle to create distance. Darkforest's final answer is also offered at the Rootheart.
world.place.workshop.story: This floor never appeared on a city tourism map. Field Supply kept unwarranted tools working; after the Reset, both the stock and the unfinished repairs remained.
world.place.workshop.tactic: Cramped, debris-strewn, and rich in cover. The shop remains here in both phases. Purchases make noise; trading is not a safe pause.
world.place.waterworks.story: Mega City took clean water for granted until the pumps stopped. Filter beds, pipe bridges, and silt did not disappear; they sank together into black water.
world.place.waterworks.tactic: Mud slows movement, and wet ground makes slipping more likely. Cover is scarce, so plan your exit before you search.
world.place.atrium.story: The upper tier turned water into decoration while hiding aging cables beneath the floor. The blast stripped away the luxury, black water flooded the furniture, and the danger finally became honest.
world.place.atrium.tactic: Open sightlines and little cover. Conductive puddles may exist in either era, but they are not revealed at first. Scanning or taking another route is the reliable choice.
world.place.archive.story: The archive compressed human lives into numbers and permissions. Darkforest never understood those categories; it simply wrapped the shelves into a tomb that still hums under its breath.
world.place.archive.tactic: Dark, tight, and full of cover. Close-range weapons and hiding gain an edge. Seeing a silhouette does not mean you know who it is.
world.place.spire.story: The council once decided from above which districts deserved to be seen. When the tower leaned, the canopy inherited that view; the long table and window frames stayed where they were.
world.place.spire.tactic: Long sightlines and usable cover coexist. Ranged weapons have room to work, but enemies have places to vanish. Trust the Preview, not distance alone.
world.place.broadcast.story: Loudspeakers once carried the same order into every street. The blast silenced them, but roots and leaves split the remaining sound into whispers with no certain source.
world.place.broadcast.tactic: It begins as a cramped, dark room and becomes a deeply overgrown dark zone. Ambushes are easier in Darkforest, making identification before attack even more important.
world.place.farm.story: The city stored seeds as disaster backups, but rarely let them touch soil. When the vault split open, its reserves became crops for the first time—and Field Supply's testimony to the future.
world.place.farm.tactic: Strong cover and concealment make this a good place to rescue, hide, or set an ambush. ROOTBOUND players can also mend a broken oath here through rescue.
world.place.stormperch.story: The weather tower once claimed it could predict everything above the city. After the Reset, only rain remained on its control panels. The tower no longer names storms; it can only endure them.
world.place.stormperch.tactic: Both eras are extremely exposed. Watch powered equipment before the blast and slick ground after it. Sparse cover makes every pause conspicuous.
world.place.well.story: Cargo was weighed and raised through the great shaft; human names survived only in handover fields. When the lifts stopped, the well kept carrying footsteps to unseen floors.
world.place.well.tactic: Open ground and darkness pull the modifiers in opposite directions, so this is not simply a ranged advantage. Cover is scarce; the Preview is your final judge.
world.place.watch.story: The barracks firing ports once divided inside from outside. After the walls fell, bunks, vines, and observation slits still teach every passerby how to hide and watch someone else.
world.place.watch.tactic: Abundant cover and hard-to-read silhouettes make this a powerful place to hide or ambush. Observe before entering; do not mistake silence for emptiness.
world.place.rail.story: The escape railway was a promise never kept. After the cars left, the tracks stayed behind to rust—and continued leading survivors toward one another.
world.place.rail.tactic: Long straightaways give ranged attacks and broad swings room, while debris hinders footwork. With little cover, both firing and rushing leave obvious traces.
world.environment.title: Terrain is not a backdrop. It is calculating you.
world.environment.body: Nine public tags affect weapons, hiding, movement, and hazards. Read the ground and silhouettes before you read the odds.
world.environment.distance.title: Distance chooses the weapon
world.environment.distance.body: Close quarters favor close-range weapons. Open ground gives ranged attacks and broad swings more room, while making it harder to disappear from sight.
world.environment.concealment.title: Out of sight does not mean empty
world.environment.concealment.body: Cover, dense growth, and darkness change hiding and identification. Read the silhouette, Signal, and Preview before choosing whether to attack.
world.environment.footing.title: The ground is fighting too
world.environment.footing.body: Wet ground, mud, and debris can slow, trip, or expose you. Footwear changes some outcomes, but it cannot erase every danger.
world.environment.energy.title: Water and power amplify each other
world.environment.energy.body: Powered infrastructure is not a trap by itself. When it shares space with standing water, a conductive hazard can form. Unknown never means safe.
world.environment.fullRules: See the Armory for every terrain modifier →
world.footer.body: Remember the scars each place keeps. Choose your route only after you enter.
world.footer.characters: Meet the people who crossed these places
about.hero.title1: The explosion does not restart the match.
about.hero.body: A no-download web battle royale that lasts up to about 30 minutes. Survive Mega City first; if you are downed before the Reset, you become an Echo, gather intel, and return to Darkforest with a different path to a comeback.
about.hero.status: NO DOWNLOAD · UP TO ~30 MIN · STARTS ON THE HOUR & HALF-HOUR
about.hero.playHint: Take a seat five minutes early, or spectate while you wait
about.hero.artAlt: One city square split by the Explosion Reset, with Mega City on the left and Darkforest on the right
about.hero.artCaption: Original environment concept: one city remembered on both sides of the Explosion Reset
about.facts.duration: Each match lasts up to about 30 minutes
about.facts.schedule: Starts on the hour and half-hour
about.facts.capacity: Up to 24 seats; AI fills empty ones
about.flow.title: You are not replaying a second match. You are surviving the same disaster.
about.flow.body: Your first-phase choices, Legacy, and story endure. Equipment is repriced by the blast as technology loses value and routes are redrawn, giving different players new leverage in the second half.
about.flow.megacity.title: Mega City: prepare before anyone else
about.flow.megacity.body: Search, move, fight—everything you do leaves a trace.
about.flow.reset.title: Explosion Reset: advantages are rewritten
about.flow.reset.body: Legacy preserves your choices. Echo turns pre-disaster intel into second-half leverage.
about.flow.darkforest.title: Darkforest: return with another way to win
about.flow.darkforest.body: Terrain and routes are remixed. Surviving alone or forming a covenant with Arbora are both contestable endings.
about.art.megacityAlt: Mega City and its red rootscape before the explosion
about.innovation.title: Not a smaller shooter—a battle royale that remembers you
about.innovation.body: Your first-half performance still matters, but it becomes room to choose—not an overwhelming advantage that makes the second half a foregone conclusion.
about.innovation.01.title: Going down before the Reset does not mean leaving
about.innovation.01.body: Eligible players become Echoes and use gathered intel to prepare their return. It is neither a free revival nor passive spectating.
about.innovation.02.title: The explosion rewrites advantages without erasing the first half
about.innovation.02.body: Legacy preserves options while equipment and routes are revalued, giving leaders flexibility and trailing players a real comeback window.
about.innovation.03.title: Low-input play, high-stakes decisions
about.innovation.03.body: The Narrative Log unifies feedback, odds appear before you act, and semi-auto policies handle repeated rhythms. You only need to rule on what truly matters.
about.innovation.04.title: Story before dashboard
about.innovation.04.body: Narrative choices, Preview → Confirm, and semi-auto policies make the next move legible. Focus on decisions instead of a wall of controls.
about.reset.title: The same place no longer follows the same rules
about.reset.body: After the city collapses, cover, routes, and hazards are rearranged. High-tech gear no longer guarantees victory, but your first-phase choices stay with you.
about.reset.beforeAlt: Mega City's Council Spire, a high-rise city node where order still operates
about.reset.afterAlt: Darkforest's Canopy Spire, the same node rewritten by roots, standing water, and darkness
about.gameplay.title: Spend less time finding buttons and more time deciding
about.gameplay.body: Characters, exits, cover, and supplies appear directly on the field. Check the odds, then choose whether to act. SEMI policies handle low-risk steps without deciding the ending for you.
about.gameplay.route.title: Choose a route
about.gameplay.route.body: Rushing is faster but loud. Moving carefully takes longer, but exposes you less.
about.gameplay.observe.title: Observe first
about.gameplay.observe.body: At a distance, you initially see only a silhouette. Move closer, wait, or gain intel to identify them.
about.gameplay.fight.title: Check the odds before firing
about.gameplay.fight.body: Hit chance, cover, equipment, and environmental modifiers are made clear before you commit.
about.gameplay.semi.title: Let SEMI handle the rhythm
about.gameplay.semi.body: Avoid, Defend, and Hunt policies reduce input pressure while leaving critical choices to you.
about.endings.title: Survive to the end—or make the world remember you
about.endings.body: The Rootheart asks not only who is alive, but what you are willing to leave behind. Both endings are public, contestable, and interruptible.
about.endings.solo.title: Claim the Rootheart
about.endings.solo.body: Declare sole ownership, then survive the final hunt while exposed to everyone.
about.endings.covenant.title: Return the memories
about.endings.covenant.body: Two or three players connect with a City Trace and Echo Memory, then defend the ritual together.
about.systems.title: AI is present, but AI never decides the winner
about.systems.01.title: Bots fill empty seats
about.systems.01.body: A match supports up to 24 seats. When there are not enough human players, AI agents fill the gaps without pretending to be human.
about.systems.02.title: Spectator delay protects the match
about.systems.02.body: After elimination, you can stay and watch the full tactical map, but delayed information prevents live intelligence from leaking back into the match.
about.systems.03.title: Arbora provides intel only
about.systems.03.body: Echoes can view fixture-backed hints in the local demo. Hints read public state only; they cannot issue actions, change values, or decide victory.
about.stack: No download · Desktop and mobile · Join live · Six-language interface
about.credits.title: One forest, three disciplines
about.credits.body: Interface, art, game rules, and the narrative model each own a different layer. Every combat outcome still resolves through deterministic rules.
about.credits.ui.name: TokimiSpace contributors
about.credits.ui.body: Maintained, reviewed, and released by TokimiSpace contributors, with AI tools used for development assistance.
about.credits.game.name: TokimiSpace
about.credits.game.body: TokimiSpace maintains the product direction and the production service that is not included in this repository.
about.credits.llm.name: Local Fixture Guide
about.credits.llm.body: Demonstrates the Echo and Arbora UI with fixed fixture responses. It contacts no external service and has no authority over combat or outcomes.
about.footer: When you are ready, enter the next match on the hour or half-hour.
about.footer.title: What will you carry through the explosion?
about.footer.body: Matches start on the hour and half-hour. Take a seat five minutes early, or spectate while you wait.

demo.notice.body: Only fixed local scenarios run. Other pages are product-concept UI snapshots. There is no online matchmaking, account, official record, persistence, or official-service compatibility.
lobby.hero.body: One match spans both sides of the blast. Fall in Mega City and return as an Echo to gather Intel; even a losing first half can turn through Insight in Darkforest.
lobby.rolesNote: All three professions enter the same disaster; each carries one fixed passive, and every match opens by drawing one match-only trait.

lobby.profile.body: Loads a local fixture directly; it creates no account, seat, or official record.

lobby.profile.humanDetail: Human · Not bound by the ROOTBOUND oath

actions.title: Field Actions
combatDecision.title: Combat Decision
tutorial.hero.body: Cross Mega City, the Explosion Reset, and Darkforest in one match. Follow five decisions through your story without memorizing the whole rulebook first.
tutorial.interface.title: Read the field, then decide
tutorial.interface.body: While alive, you never need to scroll back and forth through a long page. Status, routes, people, loot, and outcomes share one tactical cockpit.
tutorial.interface.ariaLabel: Graphical tactical interface with a return path, status bar, movement arrows, target selection, field loot, and Field or Log switching
tutorial.interface.status.title: Read your survival bars first
tutorial.interface.status.body: HP, stamina, Signal, and your held weapon stay at the top. Urgent countdowns remain in sight.
tutorial.interface.route.title: Arrows choose a destination first
tutorial.interface.route.body: Choose a direction, then pick the faster rush or quieter sneak. The arrow itself does not start travel.
tutorial.interface.target.title: Tapping a person only selects them
tutorial.interface.target.body: Odds appear automatically. Then choose Observe, Fire, or Cancel separately. Only Fire is irreversible.
tutorial.interface.scene.title: Touch field objects directly
tutorial.interface.scene.body: Loot, cover, and available actions live on the field. Icons and cooldown rings show when you can act again.
tutorial.interface.log.title: Switch between Field and Log
tutorial.interface.log.body: Use Field for the choice in front of you and Log for outcomes you are allowed to know. Global Comms is a separate chat, so no page-long scrolling is needed.
tutorial.interface.breadcrumb.title: Every subview has a way back
tutorial.interface.breadcrumb.body: Survivor, environment, action, and Log views show “← Main field / current view.” Select Main field or press Esc to return.
tutorial.interface.mobile.title: Portrait and landscape use the same controls
tutorial.interface.mobile.body: Portrait is comfortable for one-handed status checks and Log switching; landscape gives the field more room. Core actions stay fixed in both orientations.
tutorial.lesson.1.title: Read the story
tutorial.lesson.1.detail: Cross two worlds in one match
tutorial.lesson.2.title: Choose one thing
tutorial.lesson.2.detail: Make one decision at a time
tutorial.lesson.3.title: Look before striking
tutorial.lesson.4.title: Cross the blast
tutorial.lesson.4.detail: How Echo moves and comes back
tutorial.lesson.5.title: Answer the Rootheart
tutorial.footer: The match decides every chance, countdown, and outcome. Training only teaches you to read the next decision.
tutorial.back: Finish training and return to Lobby

armory.section.weapon.title: Weapons
armory.section.weapon.description: The outline alone tells you weight, reach and grip before the first shot.
armory.section.equipment.title: Equipment
armory.section.equipment.description: Six slots told apart by material, layering and bulk. The art never stands in for live match values.
armory.section.footwear.title: Footwear
armory.section.footwear.description: Sole and toe-cap silhouettes remind you the ground is part of the fight.
armory.section.supply.title: Supply and Insight
armory.section.supply.description: Medical, ammunition, repair, detection and Echo memory each keep a symbol you can read at a glance.
armory.hero.body: Browse every available weapon, armour piece, shoe, food, medical supply, and Echo item. Compare damage, accuracy, durability, terrain effects, acquisition, and what changes after Reset.
armory.loadout.caption: Six-slot paper doll · worn gear takes no pack space
armory.contact.title: Reading a fog contact
armory.contact.body: An unidentified figure reveals exactly two things: the outline of the weapon in hand, and the bulk of stacked armor. These glyphs are the same data the match renders—decide whether the fight is worth it from here.
armory.contact.weapons: Weapon outline: weight and reach leak before the first shot
armory.contact.armor: Armor bulk: light, medium, heavy—stacked from total armor value
armory.rule.progression.title: In-match level
armory.rule.progression.body: Searching, landing hits, rescuing, attuning, and surviving a Reset all earn XP; each level raises your HP cap. Levels belong only to this match and return to zero once it ends.
armory.rule.injury.title: Limb injuries
armory.rule.injury.body: Combat, slipping, and electric shock can cause a leg or arm injury. Leg injury slows movement and makes you more likely to slip; arm injury lowers your hit chance. A bandage cures one injury (legs first); a medkit cures both. Reset clears every injury.
armory.rule.shop.title: Field Supply shop
armory.rule.shop.body: The Maintenance Ring (Field Workshop after the Reset) hosts a standing shop: spend in-match cash with Field Supply for ammo, bandages, medkits, and a little armor, or sell what you don't need for cash. Cash comes from scavenging and takedowns, and it's only good this match. Featured stock is limited per match — once it's sold out, it's gone.
armory.rule.hint: Hover, focus with the keyboard, or tap to inspect the public-demo values.
armory.rule.baseNotice: The catalog shows base hit chance. Terrain, posture, exposure, cover, and fog modify it during a match.
armory.rule.footer: Card values and stat chips come directly from the current balance. Current durability, count, and state remain in the match UI.
armory.rule.guide.keyboard: Press Tab to focus, then Enter to expand
armory.rule.source.echoInsight: Insight selected by an Echo after Reset
armory.acquisition.echo_insight: Insight selected by an Echo after Reset
armory.reset.keeps: Kept unchanged even when unsealed; Legacy-sealed items also carry intact into Darkforest.
armory.reset.ammo_reduced: Unsealed ammo keeps the ratio shown on the card; Legacy-sealed ammo remains unchanged.
armory.reset.durability_reduced: Unsealed items keep the durability ratio shown on the card (minimum 1); Legacy-sealed items remain unchanged.
armory.reset.electronic_to_scrap: Unsealed electronic gear breaks down into scrap; Legacy-sealed gear remains unchanged.
armory.reset.post_reset_only: Only acquired after Reset and unaffected by the explosion conversion.
armory.item.tool.detail: It can only hit targets at the same location, and attacks normally wear down its durability.
armory.item.pistol.effect: A mobile short-range firearm with reliable aim.
armory.item.pistol.detail: It can attack the same or an adjacent location, and every shot consumes light ammo.
armory.item.rifle.effect: A long gun built to reach across a clear sightline.
armory.item.rifle.detail: It can only attack an adjacent location with line of sight, and every shot consumes light ammo.
armory.item.light_ammo.effect: General-purpose ammunition for pistols and rifles.
armory.item.light_ammo.detail: Every shot consumes ammunition; an empty weapon cannot fire.
armory.item.bandage.effect: Quickly restores a modest amount of health.
armory.item.bandage.detail: It is consumed on use, and the bandaging action must finish before healing applies.
armory.item.medkit.effect: Trades a longer opening for substantial healing.
armory.item.medkit.detail: It is consumed on use; the stronger treatment requires a safer window.
armory.item.healthy_food.detail: It is consumed on use and safely supports both survival and movement.
armory.item.spoiled_food.effect: Restores emergency stamina but causes stomach discomfort.
armory.item.spoiled_food.detail: Natural stamina regeneration stops while the discomfort lasts.
armory.item.scrap.effect: Consumes scrap to restore tool durability.
armory.item.scrap.detail: It only repairs the tool up to its durability cap; it cannot repair guns or armor.
armory.item.trap_scanner.effect: Reveals hazards at the current location.
armory.item.trap_scanner.detail: Scanning adds Signal and cannot detect distant locations.
armory.item.insight_root_sense.effect: Reveals conductive-puddle hazards at both ends of root edges.
armory.item.insight_root_sense.detail: Once locked, it accelerates Signal decay and shortens the solo finale channel; its passives remain after the active effect is used.
armory.item.insight_calamity_echo.effect: Reveals the hazard at a known location and temporarily grants immunity to it.
armory.item.insight_calamity_echo.detail: Once locked, it accelerates Signal decay and shortens the solo finale channel; its passives remain after the active effect is used.
armory.item.cloth_jacket.detail: Provides basic general damage reduction with no special resistance.
armory.item.stab_jacket.effect: Midweight protection balancing armor and durability.
armory.item.stab_jacket.detail: Provides general armor only; its name does not grant special resistance to blades or stabs.
armory.item.composite_chest.effect: The heaviest protection in the jacket slot.
armory.item.composite_chest.detail: Has the highest armor and durability in the jacket slot, with no hidden secondary effect.
armory.item.work_helmet.effect: Steady basic protection for the head.
armory.item.work_helmet.detail: Provides general armor with no environmental or search bonus.
armory.item.nvg_helmet.effect: Reduces the darkness penalty applied to ranged weapons.
armory.item.nvg_helmet.detail: Equipping it adds Signal and does not alter other environmental modifiers.
armory.item.work_pants.effect: Extra pockets provide both protection and capacity.
armory.item.work_pants.detail: They increase pack capacity with no other movement bonus.
armory.item.rough_gloves.effect: Light basic protection for the hands.
armory.item.rough_gloves.detail: Provides general armor only and does not improve search success.
armory.item.labor_gloves.effect: Adds protection while periodically reducing tool wear.
armory.item.labor_gloves.detail: During sustained tool attacks, durability loss is periodically prevented.
armory.item.leather_gloves.effect: The strongest protection in the gloves slot.
armory.item.leather_gloves.detail: Has the highest armor in the gloves slot, with no hidden secondary effect.
armory.item.small_backpack.effect: Provides a modest increase to pack capacity.
armory.item.small_backpack.detail: Provides no armor and does not change movement speed, noise, or exposure.
armory.item.large_backpack.detail: Provides no armor and does not make your silhouette more visible to distant players.
armory.item.soft_sole.effect: Improves stealth and reduces movement noise.
armory.item.soft_sole.detail: Both rushing and sneaking become quieter; shoes cannot be removed, only swapped.
armory.item.steel_toe.detail: It reduces stealth and only prevents debris slips; shoes cannot be removed, only swapped.
armory.item.tool.silhouette: Hook-jaw wrench and blunt breaching head
armory.item.pistol.silhouette: Heavy slide, trigger guard, and short grip
armory.item.rifle.silhouette: Separated stock, receiver, and long barrel
armory.item.stab_jacket.silhouette: Overlapping protective layers and raised collar
armory.item.composite_chest.silhouette: Angular vest and segmented chest plates
armory.item.work_helmet.silhouette: Hard-hat dome, ridge, and broad brim
armory.item.nvg_helmet.silhouette: Twin optical tubes and forehead mount
armory.item.work_pants.silhouette: Split legs, pockets, and knee panels
armory.item.rough_gloves.silhouette: Rough palm pads and short cuffs

tutorial.lesson.1.heading: Read the story: the blast isn't the end.
tutorial.lesson.1.intro: You wake in Mega City while the neon is still on, cross the Explosion Reset, and step into Darkforest. The blast preserves what you leave behind and rewrites the value of your gear and your route — it's always the same survival story.
tutorial.lesson.1.takeaway: Reset is a checkpoint, not a new match.
tutorial.lesson.1.visual.ariaLabel: Story timeline: Mega City through Reset into Darkforest
tutorial.lesson.1.prompt: When the blast happens, what's the most accurate way to understand it?
tutorial.lesson.1.choice.new-match.label: Start a second match
tutorial.lesson.1.choice.new-match.detai: All progress resets, and you draw a new starting hand.
tutorial.lesson.1.choice.checkpoint.labe: A turning point in the same match
tutorial.lesson.1.choice.checkpoint.deta: Keeps your story and some progress, then rewrites your gear, route, and Echo advantage.
tutorial.lesson.1.choice.cinematic.label: Just a cutscene
tutorial.lesson.1.choice.cinematic.detai: Only changes the visuals — the map and resources stay the same.
tutorial.lesson.1.success: Correct. Reset is a turning point in the same match — it preserves and rewrites.
tutorial.feedback.1.new-match: Reset isn't a second match. Traces and some progress from the same story carry forward.
tutorial.feedback.1.cinematic: Reset rewrites gear value, map routes, and Echo's return — it's not just a cutscene.
tutorial.lesson.2.heading: Choose one thing: read the situation first.
tutorial.lesson.2.intro: The graphical field shows the people, routes, and loot in front of you; switch to Log when you need the story behind them. Seeing a player doesn't mean you have to attack — only someone actually striking at you, an encounter along the way, or a berserk mode you activate yourself pushes combat to the front. No revealed hazard doesn't mean you're safe. HP is your survival line. Stamina is your travel budget — each rush costs 25, and Stealth is always available. A full ration restores both HP and Stamina; spoiled food only gives emergency Stamina and pauses natural regeneration.
tutorial.lesson.2.takeaway: Visible doesn't mean hostile. Read the field first and switch to Log for context.
tutorial.lesson.2.fact.1: HP 0 · City: become Echo / Forest: 35s wait for RESCUE
tutorial.lesson.2.prompt: You're an OATHED ROOTBOUND and just spotted an unidentified figure. What's the safest first move?
tutorial.lesson.2.choice.fire.label: Attack immediately
tutorial.lesson.2.choice.fire.detail: A friendly-fire hit still gets you BROKEN.
tutorial.lesson.2.choice.identify.label: Observe first, or check Preview
tutorial.lesson.2.choice.identify.detail: Move closer, read the Signal, then decide whether to engage.
tutorial.lesson.2.choice.identity.label: Guess identity from the figure's code
tutorial.lesson.2.choice.identity.detail: The code looks stable, so it should reveal who they are.
tutorial.lesson.2.success: Correct. If you can't identify them, don't rush to fire — ROOTBOUND friendly fire still gets you BROKEN.
tutorial.feedback.2.fire: An ROOTBOUND who hits an unidentified ally still gets BROKEN. Observe first, or read the Preview.
tutorial.feedback.2.identity: A figure's code only lets you track the same silhouette consistently — it can't reveal their true identity.
tutorial.lesson.3.heading: Look before striking: only the last step can't be undone.
tutorial.lesson.3.intro: Tapping someone you can actually see only selects them. Preview automatically shows hit chance, damage, Signal, and oath warnings. Once you've read it, only the separate Fire control makes the attack happen.
tutorial.lesson.3.takeaway: Tapping a person only selects them. Preview lets you back out; Fire is the real attack.
tutorial.lesson.3.prompt: Which order keeps Preview from being mistaken for a real attack?
Strike first, then look back at the risk.
tutorial.lesson.3.choice.target-preview-: Read hit chance, damage, Signal, and warnings first.
tutorial.lesson.3.choice.preview-auto.de: Even after Preview appears, you still have to press Fire separately.
tutorial.lesson.3.success: Correct. Preview is a forecast, not an attack — the separate Fire control is what actually strikes.
tutorial.feedback.3.attack-preview: Attack can't be undone. You must select a Target first, then get a Preview.
tutorial.feedback.3.preview-auto: Preview only lets you foresee the risk — it never fires automatically.
tutorial.lesson.4.heading: Cross the blast: Echo isn't elimination.
tutorial.lesson.4.intro: When your HP hits 0 in Mega City, you become an Echo instead of being eliminated. Every 4 seconds, an Echo can drift straight to any node on the map, ignoring roads, blockades, hazards, getting lost, and encounters along the way. It can't use in-match actions such as fighting, looting, rescuing, or changing gear, but the separate Global Chat remains available. When you reach a node you haven't attuned yet, choose "Attune here": you can Attune once every 8 seconds, usually +1 Intel the first time, or +2 if that location saw combat in the last 60 seconds before the blast. Re-attuning the same node gives +0.
tutorial.lesson.4.takeaway: Once you're an Echo, drift to new nodes and Attune — don't sit still waiting to return.
tutorial.lesson.4.visual.step1Detail: Falling in Mega City keeps you in the match
tutorial.lesson.4.visual.returnBody: It's based on where you originally fell — wherever your Echo drifts to last doesn't change your spawn point. As long as you haven't been eliminated, you can seal 1–2 Legacy items at Reset; an Echo also returns based on Intel and chooses an Insight.
tutorial.lesson.4.prompt: You've already attuned the current node. What's the best next move to improve your return?
tutorial.lesson.4.choice.repeat-attune.d: Re-attuning the same node no longer adds Intel.
tutorial.lesson.4.choice.drift-attune.la: Drift to a new node and attune
tutorial.lesson.4.choice.drift-attune.de: Moving doesn't affect your return point; only the first Attune at a new node grants Intel.
tutorial.lesson.4.choice.echo-fight.deta: An Echo can't see players and can't attack.
tutorial.lesson.4.success: Correct. Only drifting to unattuned nodes keeps adding Intel. At {target} points you can choose 2 Insight and return with 100 HP; below that, you choose 1 Insight and return with 75 HP.
tutorial.feedback.4.repeat-attune: A node only grants Intel on its first Attune. Open the node picker and drift somewhere you haven't attuned yet.
tutorial.feedback.4.echo-fight: An Echo has no player vision or combat permissions. Its comeback comes from moving and attuning.
tutorial.lesson.5.heading: Answer the Rootheart: survive alone, or return together.
tutorial.lesson.5.intro: After 17:30, once you reach the Rootheart, you can claim it alone: channel for 30 seconds, then hold your revealed position for 60 seconds. Or spend 20 seconds inviting 2–3 people to return memory together — different participants must each bring City Trace and at least 3 Echo Memory — then hold a 45-second ritual. Moving, taking damage, or going down interrupts both the channel and the ritual. The Echo Memory 3 here is the co-op eligibility threshold, not the Intel 10 threshold for a second Insight.
tutorial.lesson.5.takeaway: The Rootheart isn't an automatic ending — after 17:30, you choose to survive alone or return together.
tutorial.lesson.5.prompt: What two answers does the rule set reserve for the Rootheart?
tutorial.lesson.5.choice.solo-only.label: Only the last one counts
tutorial.lesson.5.choice.solo-only.detai: Completing the ritual together still doesn't produce a different ending.
tutorial.lesson.5.choice.two-endings.det: solo_survivor and arbora_covenant are different story endings.
tutorial.lesson.5.choice.become-npc.deta: The co-op ending turns the player into a neutral NPC.
tutorial.lesson.5.success: Correct. solo_survivor records surviving alone, and arbora_covenant records returning together — you choose at the Rootheart after 17:30.
tutorial.feedback.5.solo-only: The rules also reserve arbora_covenant — returning together is never counted as surviving alone.
tutorial.feedback.5.become-npc: The player never becomes an NPC. Arbora remains the neutral world tree — cooperation only changes the ending.
tutorial.feedback.default: That choice missed a clue in plain sight. Go back into the story and read it again.
tutorial.ui.notRecorded: Recorded only after you complete the Field Check
tutorial.progression.title: In-match level
tutorial.progression.body: Everything you do this match — searching, landing hits, rescuing, attuning, surviving the blast — earns XP. Each level raises your HP cap and heals the difference on the spot. Levels belong to this match alone: they reset to zero at the end, and everyone starts the next match at Lv1.
tutorial.perks.title: Professions and traits
tutorial.perks.body: Every profession carries one fixed passive: Couriers rush for less stamina, Scavengers search more reliably, Enforcers land meaner hits. Each match also opens by drawing one random match-only trait (Medic / Artisan / Attuned / Tough / Fleet-Footed). The combo is redrawn every match — the opening card tells you what you got this run.
tutorial.manual.quick.title: First match · 2-minute training
tutorial.manual.quick.detail: Learn to survive through five decisions
tutorial.manual.open.title: Already playing · Find one answer
tutorial.manual.open.detail: Search for shop, Echo, Signal, or a blocked control
tutorial.manual.title: Look up the problem in front of you
tutorial.manual.body: Finish the short training first, then search this manual whenever a question comes up in play. Every topic answers three things: what you will see, what to do now, and what not to assume.
tutorial.manual.searchPlaceholder: Try: shop, Echo, Signal, cannot pick up
tutorial.manual.searchEmpty: No exact match. Try a word visible on the screen, such as “shop,” “Echo,” “Signal,” or “Fire.”
tutorial.manual.timeline.title: Remember these six moments
tutorial.manual.timeline.body: The product-concept UI previews a roughly 30-minute match clock; fixture messages, not animations, own its state. The local demo does not promise a production duration.
tutorial.manual.moreStats: View live stats in the Armory
tutorial.manual.start.title: How do I enter the local demo?
tutorial.manual.start.summary: Choose presentation data and launch a fixed fixture
tutorial.manual.start.see: The public lobby provides a local-demo profile form and, when development controls are enabled, fixed scenario selection. Queue, seats, scheduled departures, and delayed spectating are product-concept presentation only.
tutorial.manual.start.do: Enter a display name, choose ROOTBOUND or Human, select a committed fixture, and start the local demo. No account is created and no other player is matched.
tutorial.manual.start.remember: Scheduled departures and assembly are product-concept presentation only. The local fixture starts immediately and provides no queue, seats, or departure timetable.
tutorial.manual.navigation.title: How do I return after opening a subview?
tutorial.manual.navigation.summary: Breadcrumbs, Field / Log tabs, and Esc return
tutorial.manual.navigation.see: Survivor, environment, action, and Log views show “← Main field / current view.” Mobile keeps Field and Log tabs at the bottom.
tutorial.manual.navigation.do: Select Main field or press Esc instead of scrolling the entire page. Your selected contact and current situation remain when you return.
tutorial.manual.navigation.remember: A subview is detail inside the same match, not an exit. If field actions disappear, find the breadcrumb before refreshing the page.
tutorial.manual.survival.title: What do HP, Stamina, and Signal control?
tutorial.manual.survival.summary: Life, action budget, and the risk of being found
tutorial.manual.survival.see: HP, Stamina, and Signal stay fixed above the field. Injuries, rushing, noise, hiding, and endgame pressure change them.
tutorial.manual.survival.do: Find treatment or healthy food when HP is low, sneak when Stamina is short, and reduce noise, hide, or leave hot routes when Signal rises.
tutorial.manual.survival.remember: Signal is not a second HP bar. The finale raises its minimum over time; once Dead Zone begins, waiting cannot return it to safety.
tutorial.manual.travel.title: Why can’t I use some routes?
tutorial.manual.travel.summary: Direction arrows, fast or quiet travel, getting lost, and blockades
tutorial.manual.travel.see: Usable exits sit on the edge of the field. Selecting an arrow reveals rush or sneak. Reset, blockades, and root traits can change routes.
tutorial.manual.travel.do: Choose a destination, then compare time, noise, and Stamina. If a silhouette appears en route, engage, observe, or continue traveling.
tutorial.manual.travel.remember: An arrow selects a destination; it does not depart immediately. Root shortcuts are slow-only, and wrong turns or loops are recorded in Log.
tutorial.manual.loot.title: Why can’t I find or pick up supplies?
tutorial.manual.loot.summary: Search, ground caches, capacity, food, and remains
tutorial.manual.loot.see: Search appears when a node can be searched; a cache appears in the scene when loot is on the ground. Capacity, brief priority, and cooldowns can block pickup.
tutorial.manual.loot.do: Check field loot and capacity first. Swap or leave an item when full. Healthy food restores HP and Stamina; spoiled food only gives emergency Stamina and discomfort.
tutorial.manual.loot.remember: A successful Search does not guarantee equipment. A fallen survivor leaves a ground cache; the downer gets only brief priority, not permanent ownership.
tutorial.manual.combat.title: How do I fight after seeing a silhouette?
tutorial.manual.combat.summary: Identification, odds Preview, Fire, and semi-automatic policy
tutorial.manual.combat.see: Unidentified players show a silhouette plus weapon and armor outlines; selection opens only Preview. SEMI also shows the current intent, engagement policy, and Next safe action.
tutorial.manual.combat.do: In manual mode, read Preview before Fire. In SEMI, choose an intent and read the next step; use Cancel to stop it, or press Esc/use any manual control to return to ASSIST immediately.
tutorial.manual.combat.remember: Preview is an estimate and hits remain random. SEMI sends only low-risk steps after the visible countdown; warnings and irreversible decisions stay manual, and every match requires re-enabling.
tutorial.manual.growth.title: What do level, profession, trait, and injuries change?
tutorial.manual.growth.summary: Match growth, a fixed passive, a random trait, and body-part injuries
tutorial.manual.growth.see: Your dossier shows Lv, XP, profession, match trait, and arm or leg injuries. Another player’s level appears only after identification.
tutorial.manual.growth.do: Searching, hitting, rescuing, Attuning, and surviving Reset earn XP. Adapt to this run’s passive, and treat injuries or choose lower-risk actions.
tutorial.manual.growth.remember: Level and the random trait last only for this match; profession belongs to your profile. Leg injuries change movement, arm injuries change combat—HP is not the whole story.
tutorial.manual.shop.title: Where are the Field Supply shop controls?
tutorial.manual.shop.summary: They appear only after you physically reach Field Supply’s shop node
tutorial.manual.shop.see: The map marks the shop node. While there, the scene reveals Field Supply, cash, catalog, buy and sell prices, and stock.
tutorial.manual.shop.do: Open scene trading at the shop, choose an item, and read the confirmation before buying or selling. Low cash, full capacity, and sold-out stock explain themselves.
tutorial.manual.shop.remember: You do not need to wait for other players to leave, and you cannot shop remotely from every node. Trading makes noise and shares a short cooldown.
tutorial.manual.reset.title: What do I do at 0 HP or after becoming Echo?
tutorial.manual.reset.summary: Mega City keeps you in play through Legacy, Attune, and return
tutorial.manual.reset.see: Falling in Mega City changes the interface to monochrome Echo view. Reset presents Legacy and Insight choices according to your state.
tutorial.manual.reset.do: Drift to un-Attuned nodes and use Attune to gather Intel. During Reset, preserve valuable gear as Legacy, then choose your return Insight.
tutorial.manual.reset.remember: Echo cannot fight or loot, but can move and Attune; your last drift does not change the return location. Falling in Darkforest uses rescue and elimination instead. Global Comms is a separate channel.
tutorial.manual.finale.title: How does a match end?
tutorial.manual.finale.summary: Last standing, two Rootheart endings, and Dead Zone
tutorial.manual.finale.see: Late blockades drive players toward Rootheart. When eligible, high-priority choices offer solo claim, shared return, join, or interrupt.
tutorial.manual.finale.do: For solo survival, defend the public Rootheart channel. For shared return, bring different memory sources and protect the ritual. You can also interrupt another channel.
tutorial.manual.finale.remember: Rootheart is not an automatic win. A match may also end by last standing, total loss, or timed judgment; Dead Zone forces everyone to answer.
tutorial.manual.communication.title: What is the difference between Log, Combat Record, and Global Comms?
tutorial.manual.communication.summary: Match causality, personal combat, and player chat stay separate
tutorial.manual.communication.see: Narrative Log keeps match causes you may know; Combat Record stays on fights involving you or your location; Global Comms is an independent chat.
tutorial.manual.communication.do: Keep immediate actions in Field and switch to Log for results and clues. Open Global Comms to talk, and translate individual messages only when needed.
tutorial.manual.communication.remember: Chat does not change combat rules or enter Narrative Log automatically. Distant fights obey fog and leave only knowable clues such as gunfire or screams.

characters.hero.eyebrow: SURVIVOR DOSSIERS · THREE WAYS TO LIVE
characters.hero.title2: Three ways to survive a world ending.
characters.hero.body: These files are profession archetypes and lenses on the world. Your name, ROOTBOUND/Human affiliation, and victory lines remain yours; a match trait is drawn again at the start of every game.
characters.chronicle.title: Complete survival record
characters.role.scavenger.alt: A scavenger in an asymmetric olive rain cape and salvage harness
characters.role.scavenger.title: Scavenger
characters.role.scavenger.epithet: The one who remembers what the lost was called
characters.role.scavenger.tagline: Find proof worth keeping in what the city threw away.
characters.role.scavenger.quote: “Not everything should be carried away. But everything once belonged to someone.”
characters.role.scavenger.ability: +4% search success chance (applied before the probability cap)
characters.role.scavenger.abilityBody: Your searches more often become real supplies, but never guarantee a rare drop.
characters.role.scavenger.approach: Read capacity, terrain, and an exit before you search, re-equip, or seal a Legacy.
characters.role.scavenger.risk: One more chance to search can also mean one more moment exposed at a sought-after supply point.
characters.role.scavenger.story.1.title: The last page in the recovery catalogue
characters.role.scavenger.story.1.body: You once logged unclaimed objects for Mega City's municipal recovery system. The people above cared only about weight and residual value. You wrote down each find site, each mark left by an owner, and every final destination on the back of its disposal tag. When evacuation lists began missing people, your private catalogue became the undercity's most dependable memory of who had lived there.
characters.role.scavenger.story.2.title: To preserve is not to possess
characters.role.scavenger.story.2.body: When the alarm sounded, you returned to Waterworks with the catalogue, looking for an ID fragment that could still prove an entire block had existed. The blast melted serial numbers and split preservation from possession: the thing you sealed was not your dearest tool, but a label whose name could no longer be read.
characters.role.scavenger.story.3.title: Let the ruins testify for the vanished
characters.role.scavenger.story.3.body: In Darkforest, metal replays broken sounds beneath rootlight. You search by those echoes, put useful things back into living hands, and trace why the Reset happened. Each success asks the same question: keep the supplies for yourself now, or keep the evidence for people who may have no tomorrow.
characters.role.scavenger.conflict: You fear that one day you will stop being a keeper and become someone merely better at excusing hoarding.
characters.role.enforcer.alt: An enforcer in dark heavy protective gear with a weathered red shoulder plate
characters.role.enforcer.title: Enforcer
characters.role.enforcer.epithet: The one who carries the consequence of every strike
characters.role.enforcer.tagline: After order breaks, facing danger does not mean obeying an order.
characters.role.enforcer.quote: “Accuracy is not courage. Knowing when not to pull the trigger is.”
characters.role.enforcer.abilityBody: The profession modifier appears in Combat Preview. It improves accuracy; it does not increase weapon damage.
characters.role.enforcer.approach: Identify the threat, read the odds, then make every strike a decision you can carry.
characters.role.enforcer.risk: Reliable hits can tempt an early fight; a silhouette may still be a stranger who never meant to fight.
characters.role.enforcer.story.1.title: The final cordon
characters.role.enforcer.story.1.body: You were a field enforcer in danger zones. Your work was to take people away from failing infrastructure, not decide who stayed beyond a gate. The city made the red shoulder plate a symbol of command; you knew it truly carried shoves, shrapnel, and choices that could not be explained in time.
characters.role.enforcer.story.2.title: After the orders went silent
characters.role.enforcer.story.2.body: Thirty seconds before the Explosion Reset, the command channel died before the alarm. You broke the cordon order and opened a gate for the last group, never learning whether they made it through. The blast consumed the handover record. From that moment, you could only sign your own judgment.
characters.role.enforcer.story.3.title: Between protection and control
characters.role.enforcer.story.3.body: Darkforest has no complete chain of command, only root-split paths and silhouettes without a readable identity. You still stand where pressure is worst, but have begun to treat observation as another kind of courage. A precise shot can save a route, and can just as quietly turn protection into control.
characters.role.enforcer.conflict: You have to prove again and again that strength can shield others from danger without deciding their fate for them.
characters.role.courier.alt: A courier in a deep-navy long coat with a diagonal route harness
characters.role.courier.title: Courier
characters.role.courier.epithet: The one who carries undelivered words across a fault line
characters.role.courier.tagline: Roads vanish. As long as someone waits, direction does not.
characters.role.courier.quote: “Speed is not the point. Giving something a chance to arrive is.”
characters.role.courier.abilityBody: With a leg injury, rush costs 27. This is a profession discount, not the move cooldown of a Courier background.
characters.role.courier.approach: Spend the saved stamina to reroute, rescue someone, or break contact; fast and slow movement still carry distinct noise costs.
characters.role.courier.risk: Reaching the destination and stopping to help can be two betrayals made in the same second.
characters.role.courier.story.1.title: The last undelivered sentence
characters.role.courier.story.1.body: You carried messages between disconnected districts without using the city network. You remembered routes but kept no addressee list; you confirmed a sentence had arrived but never asked whom it might change. When Mega City's communications were sealed zone by zone, people still knew one another lived by the sound of your steps.
characters.role.courier.story.2.title: The map failed. Direction remained.
characters.role.courier.story.2.body: Before the blast, you raced toward Council Spire with an unsigned message. The shockwave turned familiar shortcuts into fault lines; a paper map became a false promise. What you sealed was a way of reading wind, echoes, and exits. If you became an Echo, that was the first time you saw how disaster could stitch roads together anew.
characters.role.courier.story.3.title: Arrival is not escape
characters.role.courier.story.3.body: In Darkforest, roots rename roads and silhouettes make every rendezvous risky. You still carry supplies, directions, and news of the living, because arrival has never been only escape: it lets two people who would have missed each other choose again.
characters.role.courier.conflict: You fear not arriving late, but missing someone who needed you to stop because you had to arrive on time.
characters.traits.title: A profession defines the method. A trait rewrites this match.
characters.traits.body: One of five traits is drawn at the opening. It never accumulates permanently and is not revealed to other players; the affinities in these files are play advice, not locked pairings.
characters.trait.medic.label: Medic
characters.trait.medic.effect: +20% healing from bandages and medkits; food does not receive the bonus.
characters.trait.artisan.label: Artisan
characters.trait.artisan.effect: One out of every four tool swings does not spend durability.
characters.trait.attuned.label: Attuned
characters.trait.attuned.effect: +1 Intel from your first Attune; Echo movement cooldown ×0.75.
characters.trait.tough.label: Tough
characters.trait.tough.effect: +10 maximum HP, and begin at the new full-health maximum.
characters.trait.fleet.label: Fleet
characters.trait.fleet.effect: Movement cooldown ×0.92; slip chance is halved.
characters.world.title: They answer the world. They do not decide a player's result.
characters.world.supply.story: A stationary supply terminal demonstrates how the client presents buying, selling, prices, and limited stock after arrival. All data comes from a local fixture; no production service or unreleased NPC content is included.
characters.world.supply.can: Presents the local fixture catalog, prices, stock, and trade states.
characters.world.supply.cannot: Does not represent production characters, content, balance, or service contracts.
characters.world.arbora.alt: Arbora rising above the ruins of Darkforest
characters.world.arbora.role: Neutral world tree, witness to echoes
characters.world.arbora.story: Mega City treated signals from the underground roots as infrastructure noise. Only after the Explosion Reset did people call the presence that preserves disaster echoes Arbora. It speaks for no faction; at Echo, Attunement, and Rootheart, it only rearranges memories that already exist for you to see.
characters.world.arbora.can: Answers an Echo's voluntary questions; at Rootheart, accepts the shared return of memory from 2–3 qualified players.
characters.world.arbora.cannot: Has no authority over attacks, actions, drops, values, or victory, and never chooses a side for a player.
characters.identity.title: The archetype gives you a method. You leave the name and oath.
characters.identity.body: ROOTBOUND is a human cultural oath, not an animal, a good-or-evil faction, or a fixed team; Human is not a villain either. Players cannot become NPCs. Once you choose a name and affiliation, the city lets your profession and match trait become part of the same story.
characters.identity.rootbound: The kin oath asks for restraint, while still allowing broken relationships to be redeemed through rescue.
characters.identity.retaliation: Only after you have first been attacked can retaliation make those words true.
characters.identity.cta: Create a survivor and wait for the next run
